original_card.first_experiment: Choose one assumption ID (native_all_columns, owned_erasure, compiler, precision_tape, analytic_recovery), one quantified implication and exact dependency closure. Check current handoffs, including #5625 row reentry and #5707 root-prefix lowering, without treating their partial scope as the whole theorem. actual_scope: Open question 1 of #6312 (research/mode-preserving-rounding, head 46593234bfe658b63fb829f0d22b7eb216e392a2): the least uniform l_inf radius R for exact mode-preserving integer rounding on all nonempty fibers of the PR4933 mode map M.
scope_change_reason: The session drew recursive-interfaces cards needing a full construction context. #6312 had just changed this card to a precision side result and left its first open question with only a lower bound. That self-contained question is answered here in part.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the precision contract of the coded inverse. It bounds what an exact mode-preserving rounder can achieve on this M; it does not show that any caller needs one.
stop_rule: Stop at a rigorous characterisation plus explicit upper bounds, or at one exact counterexample t in L cap int Z outside S. Do not claim R = 1 from search evidence.
evidence: PROOF.md Theorems A, B and C, with verify.py exact checks: L is the Hamming E8 lattice; the genericity rank condition; the tau = 6 basis; the pinned blocks and 2e_j pairs; the exhaustive Hall lemma; 120 exact runs of the Theorem C rounder; 1,864 exact subset-sum witnesses.

open_questions.question: Is every lattice point of L in the open zonotope int Z a 0/1 subset sum of rows (equivalently, R = 1)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It settles #6312's open question exactly; the search sample supports yes.
open_questions.first_step: Use the signed-permutation automorphism group of the 112 rows to reduce the finitely many near-boundary cases. Try a face recursion: points deep in Z are handled by discrepancy rounding, and points near a face reduce to the rows lying in that flat.
open_questions.blocked_by: Brute force is infeasible (roughly 1e12 lattice points), and the face recursion is not proved.

open_questions.question: Can R <= 2 be lowered towards 1?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Theorem C loses one unit through the vertex step; an exact stress test of 12,000 inputs reaches 1.998, so the construction itself is tight at 2.
open_questions.first_step: Replace the vertex y* with a fiber point near y, for example by blockwise Beck-Fiala rounding against the 8 mode constraints, then reuse the pair-and-Hall repair.
open_questions.blocked_by: The repair must fit in the remaining error budget per coordinate.
